rtpbuddy.map.tip.fit: Zoom to fit every visible sample (F). Hold shift to fit the whole world border instead
rtpbuddy.map.tip.export: Write the visible samples to a timestamped CSV
rtpbuddy.map.tip.panels: Show or hide the side panels (Tab)
rtpbuddy.map.tip.settings: All settings: capture, auto-RTP, guards, map (O)
rtpbuddy.map.tip.auto: Starts the loop, or stops it outright. The auto-RTP key holds and continues instead; End always stops.
rtpbuddy.map.tip.splitter: Drag to resize the panel - double-click resets it
rtpbuddy.map.detail.hint: C copy   Del delete   Ctrl+Z undo
rtpbuddy.session.heading: This session
rtpbuddy.all.status.comparing: comparing sessions (right-click a row to change)
rtpbuddy.settings.subtitle: Hover a control to see what it does
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.preset_done: regions reset to the bundled preset
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.manual_step.tip: The run sends nothing on its own - every teleport waits for a key press. The rotation, the counters, the caps and every stop condition stay exactly as configured; only the moment is yours. Cooldown and jitter no longer apply.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.manual_note: Stepped by hand: cooldown and jitter are out of force. The auto-RTP key sends the next teleport, at least %s seconds after the last one. End still stops.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.gap_note: Gap mode shades up to the 5k scale and counts tiles beyond it. The tile size holds to 100k, then grows again.
rtpbuddy.auto_dialog.will_send_manual: Sends %s - by hand, one teleport per key press
rtpbuddy.auto_dialog.stops: Stops on damage, on disconnect, and after %s
rtpbuddy.auto_dialog.on_player: Stops from the first landing on, as soon as another player is closer than %s blocks.
rtpbuddy.auto_dialog.never: Never shortens a cooldown, never restarts itself.
rtpbuddy.capture.not_in_world: cannot capture: not in a world
rtpbuddy.auto.step_idle: RTPBuddy: no run active - start auto-RTP first
rtpbuddy.auto.step_timed: RTPBuddy: this run is on the clock, not by hand
rtpbuddy.auto.step_held: RTPBuddy: the run is held - continue it first
rtpbuddy.auto.step_capturing: RTPBuddy: the last landing is still being recorded
rtpbuddy.auto.step_too_soon: RTPBuddy: %ss to go before the next one
rtpbuddy.reason.region_no_command: the configured region has no command
rtpbuddy.chat.auto_paused: RTPBuddy: auto-RTP held after %s teleports - the same key continues
rtpbuddy.chat.auto_pause_idle: RTPBuddy: no auto-RTP run to hold
rtpbuddy.cmd.help.3: /rtpbuddy auto status | start | stop | pause | resume
rtpbuddy.cmd.export.failed: RTPBuddy: export failed, see the log
rtpbuddy.cmd.auto.running_manual: Auto-RTP: running by hand, %s sent, for %s - the auto-RTP key sends the next one
rtpbuddy.cmd.auto.running: Auto-RTP: running, next in %ss, %s sent, up %s
rtpbuddy.map.hint.keys: Tab panels   F fit   Shift+F border   R reset   C copy
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.enabled.tip: Master switch for automatic recording. Off means typed commands are no longer watched and no new samples appear. Existing data is untouched, and manual capture with K still works.
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.auto.tip: Whether a matching command arms a recording. Off leaves only the K hotkey.
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.dimension.tip: Counts a dimension change during the wait as a successful teleport. This is the switch for /rtp nether and /rtp end, where the horizontal jump can be tiny.
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.reject.tip: Throws away a landing whose jump stayed below the threshold in the same dimension. Stops a refused RTP from becoming a data point.
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.csv.tip: Keeps rtp_samples.csv in step with the JSON. The JSON is authoritative; the CSV is convenience for Excel.
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.threshold.tip: How far you must move horizontally before it counts as a teleport. Too low and elytra flight triggers it; too high and near RTPs are missed.
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.arm_timeout.ti: How long to wait for the teleport after the command. Raise it if the server has a countdown before it teleports you.
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.settle.tip: How long the position must stay still after landing before the sample is taken. Keeps a server correction from being recorded as the final spot.
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.debounce.tip: Collects writes so a burst of RTPs is a single save. 0 writes at once.
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.preset.tip: Resets the region list to the bundled overworld / nether / end preset. Use it if the patterns in config.json got broken.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.start.tip: Opens the start dialog. It names the rotation, the wait and every stop condition; nothing is sent before you press start.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.pause.tip: Holds the loop without ending the run. Counters, rotation position and the wait that was left all stay put. Also on the auto-RTP key and /rtpbuddy auto pause.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.resume.tip: Continues a held run with the wait it had left when you held it. Also on the auto-RTP key and /rtpbuddy auto resume.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.region.tip: Which configured region the loop asks for. The command actually sent is shown on the right.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.cooldown.tip: Gap between two teleports, typed in seconds. Set it to your server's own cooldown or higher - it never shortens one. Anything under 2 s is raised to 2 s.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.jitter.tip: A random 0 to n seconds added to every cooldown so the spacing is not machine-exact. 0 turns it off.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.rate_note: Both in seconds, typed freely. The cooldown is never run below %d s, and it is measured between landings rather than between sends.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.stop_after.tip: Stops the loop after this long. No limit means it runs until something stops it.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.max.tip: Stops after this many teleports in one run.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.wait.tip: Does not send the next command until the previous landing has been recorded.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.on_damage.tip: Stops the moment you take damage - the usual sign of a bad landing.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.on_guards.tip: Stops when a landing falls inside a guard band, near the border or spawn.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.on_player.tip: Ends the run as soon as another player turns up inside the radius. It only takes effect once the run has teleported you away, or a stop would leave you unable to start the run that gets you away from that very player. The client only knows the players the server sends it, so anyone outside the server's tracking range, and anyone it is hiding, is not seen here. A reason to stop, not a promise that you are alone.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.player_radius.tip: How close another player has to be to count, measured in three dimensions. Setting it beyond the server's tracking range buys nothing, because players further out never reach the client at all.
rtpbuddy.settings.guards.border_radius.t: How far the world border sits from 0,0. Drawn on the map and used to judge whether a landing is near the edge.
rtpbuddy.settings.guards.nether_border_r: The nether's own border, if it differs from the overworld's - most servers make it smaller. 0 means it uses the overworld radius. Each dimension's border is drawn on the map in that dimension's colour.
rtpbuddy.settings.guards.end_border_radi: The end's own border, if it differs from the overworld's. 0 means it uses the overworld radius.
rtpbuddy.settings.guards.border_guard.ti: Width of the warning band just inside the border.
rtpbuddy.settings.guards.spawn_x.tip: X of the spawn point the guard ring is drawn around.
rtpbuddy.settings.guards.spawn_z.tip: Z of the spawn point the guard ring is drawn around.
rtpbuddy.settings.guards.spawn_guard.tip: Radius around spawn that counts as too close.
rtpbuddy.settings.guards.square.tip: Treat the border as a square, the way vanilla does, instead of a circle.
rtpbuddy.settings.guards.use_position.ti: Copies where you are standing into Spawn X and Spawn Z.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.hud.tip: The small status overlay in the corner while you play.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.remember.tip: Keeps pan and zoom between visits instead of fitting to the data every time.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.grid.tip: The coordinate grid behind the samples.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.player.tip: Shows where you are, with your facing.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.last_leg.tip: Draws the red line from the point the last teleport started at to the point it landed on, with an arrow pointing the way it went. Watching the map, it answers which of the dots you just came from without clicking one. Left out across dimensions.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.numbers.tip: Prints the sample number next to each point.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.scale_bar.tip: The distance scale in the corner of the map.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.density_cell.tip: Edge length of one density cell. It no longer draws anything; it is the basis of the coverage statistic - cells hit divided by the cells inside the border. Smaller is finer but pushes the percentage down, so pin the size before comparing.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.gap_mask_tile.tip: Tile size the map uses to mark off where anything has been recorded at all. Bigger lets the search look further past the outermost landings.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.gap_raster_tile.ti: How much ground one counted tile covers. Every size divides a server region evenly, and the tiles are counted from the world border — so none of them ever lies across a region line or over the world edge. Smaller is more exact; past a 100k scale bar the growing tile takes over again.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.gap_top.tip: How many holes the map rings and lists in the column.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.panel_reset.tip: Puts both side panels back to their default width.
rtpbuddy.map.tip.scope: What the map plots: this session or every session ever recorded
rtpbuddy.settings.map.fps_limit.tip: Minecraft does not slow a screen down while a world is behind it, so the map redraws as fast as your video setting allows. A still picture does not need that, and the spare frames only heat the CPU.
rtpbuddy.map.gaps.title: Biggest gaps
rtpbuddy.map.tip.sidebar: Drag to divide the sidebar between the sessions and the samples
rtpbuddy.settings.map.legend.tip: The small panel in the corner of the plot saying what the marker colours stand for - the regions, dimensions or sessions currently on screen.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.server_regions.tip: DonutSMP splits its overworld into 81 cells of 50,000 blocks and gives each one to one of six server regions - NA East, EU Central, Asia and so on. This paints those cells under the plot in the colour of the region that owns them, so you can see which region a landing belongs to. Shown only for samples recorded on a server that uses the grid.
rtpbuddy.map.tip.delete: Delete the picked sample (Del). Shift-drag a rectangle to pick several, Ctrl+Z undoes it
rtpbuddy.map.status.delete_nothing: Nothing picked - click a sample or shift-drag a rectangle
rtpbuddy.dialog.delete.title: Delete %s samples?
rtpbuddy.dialog.delete.body: Removes %s recordings (#%s to #%s) from the file. Ctrl+Z on the map undoes it once; after that it is gone.
rtpbuddy.hud_layout.hint: Drag a box or use the arrow keys (shift = 10 px); Tab switches element. It snaps to the edges and the centre.
rtpbuddy.hud.preview_status: Preview - this is how it looks in game
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.enabled.tip: The small status overlay in the corner while you play.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.place.tip: Opens a screen where the HUD and the minimap are dragged into place with the mouse, with the rest of the HUD visible behind them.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.place_note: Both positions are stored as a corner plus an offset, so they stay put when the window is resized or the GUI scale changes.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.anchor.tip: Which corner of the screen the overlay hangs from. The offsets below are measured inwards from it.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.scale.tip: Scales the whole overlay, independently of the game's GUI scale.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.opacity.tip: How solid the plate behind the text is.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.shadow.tip: Readability with the plate switched off.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.round_markers.tip: Draws landings as discs rather than squares, in every view.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.marker_size.tip: Diameter of one marker in pixels. Small keeps a crowded patch readable; large keeps single landings visible when zoomed right out.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.reopen: Reopen the map after a teleport
rtpbuddy.settings.map.reopen.tip: A teleport across worlds brings up the game's own loading screen, which throws away whatever was open. This puts the map back afterwards, at the same scope and view.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.reopen_note: Escape still closes the map for good; only what the game itself took away comes back.
rtpbuddy.map.tip.undo: Puts the samples from the last deletion back (Ctrl+Z). Only the most recent deletion can be undone.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.region_row.tip: Sends /%s. With several regions on, each teleport takes the next one.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.order.tip: Round robin walks the list in order; random picks one each time.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.rotation_none: No region selected - nothing will be sent.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.pause_note: Holding does not end the run: nothing is sent, the clock stands still, and damage or guards stop nothing while it holds.
rtpbuddy.settings.auto.pause_note_held: Held after %s teleports. Nothing is sent until you continue.
rtpbuddy.settings.capture.unknown.tip: Also records an /rtp whose destination is missing from the region list. The argument is kept verbatim as the region.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.remember_filter.ti: Dimension, region and capture mode stay set the next time the map opens.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.hide_empty_session: Sittings without a single landing are left out of the list.
rtpbuddy.all.resume_pick_one: Pick exactly one session, then continue it
rtpbuddy.all.resume_other_server: %s belongs to another server - cannot be continued
rtpbuddy.all.merge_other_server: Sessions from different servers cannot be merged
rtpbuddy.all.merge_confirm.body: %d sessions holding %d landings between them become one. The target is the oldest, started %s — its colour, name and start time stay. Nothing is deleted: every landing survives and they then count from 1 in the order you actually landed. The other session records go, and that cannot be undone.
rtpbuddy.all.rename_pick_one: Pick exactly one session, then rename it
rtpbuddy.all.rename_hint: A name for this sitting, up to 32 characters. It replaces %s in the list, in the session card and in the viewer. Leave it empty to clear it and get the server name back.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.row_context.tip: A row under the last landing carrying its biome and dimension.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.player_pulse.tip: A slow ring fading out around your position. Motion is the one channel nothing else on the plot uses, so the marker is found at once after a teleport.
rtpbuddy.map.status.new_session: New sitting started - samples count from 1 again
rtpbuddy.map.status.new_session_empty: This sitting has not recorded a landing yet
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.enabled.tip: The small map at the edge of the screen. It frames the same rectangle the full map's "fit" picks, with your own position inside it.
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.size.tip: Edge length of the square plate in GUI pixels. From about 104 px the server cell numbers fit inside it.
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.opacity.tip: How far the plate covers the world behind it. The rim stays visible either way, so a faint plate still has an edge.
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.scope.tip: Which landings the minimap frames: this sitting only, or everything ever recorded.
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.note: The frame is fixed - it holds exactly the chosen landings. Walk out of that rectangle and you are pinned to the rim as a yellow dot. With nothing recorded the minimap frames the server cell you are standing in instead.
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.regions.tip: The server's 50 000 block cells, each in the colour of the region that owns it. The cell you are standing in is the bright one.
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.cell_numbers.t: Writes the server number into each cell. Skipped while the cells are too small to hold one.
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.axes.tip: The two lines through x = 0 and z = 0.
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.last_leg.tip: The red line into the newest landing: where that teleport started.
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.caption: Caption
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.caption.tip: The strip under the plate naming the region and cell you are standing in, and how wide the framed area is.
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.reset_done: Minimap put back to its defaults.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.background.tip: The dark plate behind the text. Off leaves the text alone — then the text shadow earns its keep, or the readout disappears over pale ground.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.offset_x.tip: Distance inwards from the chosen corner, in GUI pixels. Place the overlays is easier: there you drag the box to where it belongs.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.offset_y.tip: Distance inwards from the chosen corner, in GUI pixels. Place the overlays is easier: there you drag the box to where it belongs.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.reset.tip: Puts the text overlay's corner, offsets, size, plate and text shadow back to their defaults. The row switches are left as they are.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.row_auto.tip: The row with the countdown and the number of commands sent. It only appears while an auto-RTP run exists.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.row_state.tip: The row with the capture state: watching, armed with the time left, landing, or paused.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.row_counters.tip: The row with the counters: captured this sitting, stored in total, missed and rejected.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.row_last.tip: The block for the last landing: its number and region in that region's colour, with the coordinates and the distance from origin underneath.
rtpbuddy.settings.hud.row_status.tip: Short capture messages, visible for six seconds — why a sample was rejected, for instance.
rtpbuddy.settings.minimap.reset.tip: Puts the minimap's corner, offsets, edge length and opacity back to their defaults. What it draws stays as you set it.
rtpbuddy.map.tip.biome: Opens the list of biome families the chosen scope actually holds, each with its colour and its count. One click picks, a click beside it closes, so does Esc. Cycling eighteen families would not be a filter: after the wrong pick there would be seventeen clicks between you and all of them again. A single biome is what the search box is for - it matches both the id and the name the game shows.
rtpbuddy.stats.cells_none: None of these landings sits on a cell grid.
rtpbuddy.chat.new_cell: New cell #%s. That is %s of %s cells reached.
rtpbuddy.auto_dialog.find: It stops as soon as a landing matches: %s.
rtpbuddy.auto_dialog.find_cap: Gives up on its own after %s landings with no match.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.enabled.tip: Every other stop ends a run because something went wrong. This one ends it because the run found what it was sent out for: it keeps teleporting until a landing matches, stops on that landing and says which condition fired. It never sends more or faster - a search order can only end a run earlier than it would have ended anyway.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.off_note: Off. The run only stops for the usual reasons: damage, the run timer, the cap, a guard, a nearby player.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.new_cell.tip: Stops on the first landing in a cell no recorded landing has ever reached. This is the condition that fills the cell board - exactly the teleports that get you somewhere.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.cells.tip: Stops only in the cells you list here. Empty means this condition does not count.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.cells_hint: Cell numbers separated by spaces or commas, 1 to %s. For instance "11 12 20". Leaving it empty switches the condition off.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.min_distance.tip: Stops only when the landing is at least this far from the origin. 0 switches the lower bound off.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.max_distance.tip: Stops only when the landing is at most this far from the origin. 0 means no upper bound.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.near_x.tip: X of the point the run should stop near. Only takes effect with a radius above 0.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.near_z.tip: Z of the point the run should stop near. Only takes effect with a radius above 0.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.near_radius.tip: Stops as soon as a landing falls closer than this to the target point. 0 switches the condition off.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.use_position.tip: Takes your current position as the target point. With no radius set yet it is put at 500 blocks.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.family_row.tip: Opens the biome list of the %s family. The whole family sits at the top, and below it every single biome with the number of landings already recorded in it - a 0 means the search has never been there. Several biomes at once are allowed; the menu stays open while you tick them.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.biomes_note: Clicking a family opens its biomes. The whole family stops on any landing in its colour; a single biome stops only there - "Pale Garden" rather than "something rare". The list comes from the server's own biome registry, so it also holds biomes you have never landed in.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.match.tip: Whether one satisfied condition is enough or they all have to hold at once. All together gets rare quickly - that is when the give-up cap earns its keep.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.give_up.tip: Ends the run after this many landings with no match. With no cap a search order for a rare target runs until something else stops it.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.sound.tip: Plays a short bell when the search order fires. The whole point of a search order is not having to watch, so the ending has to arrive without a look at the screen.
rtpbuddy.settings.find.none_note: No condition chosen. The search order is on, but it is looking for nothing.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.cell_board.tip: The nine-by-nine board at the top of the metrics column. It answers what the coverage figure below it cannot: that one divides by a disc whose size depends on the cell edge you set, the board counts against 81 fixed cells.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.cell_board_numbers: Writes the number into every cell that holds a landing. Off leaves the colour blocks alone - quieter, and easier to read in a narrow column.
rtpbuddy.cmd.help.5: /rtpbuddy cells shows the cell progress, /rtpbuddy find the search order.
rtpbuddy.cmd.cells.head: Cells: %s of %s reached, %s of them only once.
rtpbuddy.cmd.cells.here: You are standing in cell #%s with %s landings.
rtpbuddy.cmd.find.empty: Search order is on, but no condition is chosen.
rtpbuddy.cmd.find.cap: Gives up after %s landings with no match.
rtpbuddy.cmd.find.progress: This run has turned down %s landings so far.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.density_budget.tip: How many markers may be on screen at once before the map draws the cheap way. Every rectangle allocates twice on 1.21.11, and two thousand framed landings is ten thousand rectangles for the dots alone. Over the budget only one marker per marker-sized patch is drawn - the ones left out were underneath another one anyway. If that is still not enough, markers inside the clusters go square instead of round; lone dots and the picked marker always keep their shape. Off draws every landing however many there are.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.density_note: Thins above %s visible markers. Below that nothing changes.
rtpbuddy.settings.map.density_note_off: Off: every landing is drawn on its own. With many landings visible at once that costs noticeable frame rate.
